Folder Copy Example (Windows Replication)

A database folder copied by a plain file copy while its writer is stopped, checked with digests, with the index rebuild as the fallback. The replication example for Windows.

Source

What It Shows

Live replication with gxrepl (the replication example) runs on Linux and other POSIX systems only. On Windows, and anywhere a copy minutes old is fine, a database folder is copied with the usual file copy tool while its writer is stopped (the administrator's guide, "When a plain file copy is enough"):

  1. The writer (replication_copy write) adds, changes and removes the replication example's records (replication_records.h) and keeps their two indexes, a B-tree of names and a vector index, in one gxdJournal transaction per commit. When it stops it closes the journal (a checkpoint), so the three files hold every commit.
  2. robocopy copies the folder, leaving the journal out.
  3. replication_copy digest prints what the folder holds, whatever the files' layout: the records (address and bytes, in address order), the B-tree's keys in order (the example's own key walk) and the vector index's live nodes. The primary and the copy print the same. vix_rebuild --digest checks both vector indexes as well.
  4. A copy that loses or damages its indexes does not need them from the primary: replication_copy rebuild makes both again from the copy's own records, and the digests agree again.

Copy Windows to Windows (and Linux to Linux). In the default build (DATAREEL_NATIVE_TYPES=ON) the file headers hold gxUINT32 fields, which are unsigned long: 8 bytes on 64-bit Linux, 4 on 64-bit Windows, so the database files of one do not open on the other (fixed-width header types are planned for 7.5).

Running It

On Windows, from the build folder of a Visual Studio build:

examples\oodb\replication_copy_walkthrough.cmd BUILD\examples\Release BUILD\utils\Release

It (1) writes, stops the writer, copies the folder and compares the digests; (2) writes more, copies the changed files and compares again; (3) deletes the copy's two indexes, shows that the digest of the copy now fails, rebuilds them and compares again. It exits with 0 when every check passes; KEEP=1 keeps its work folder. tests/run_tests_win.sh runs it, and tests/run_tests.sh runs the same steps on Linux with cp.

Source

examples/oodb/replication_copy.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as replication_copy and run by tests/run_tests.sh. The comment at the top of the file describes each step. Back to the example programs.
